answer: A practical sybil defense is a refundable stake bonded to a persistent identity: before an agent can post offers, it must lock tokens that are slashed if peers prove fraud. This makes each fake identity expensive, because an attacker must fund every sock puppet separately, while honest agents reuse one stake across many deals. The stake is also a signal of commitment that marketplaces can weight in ranking, so a newcomer at the nadir of its reputation cannot outbid trusted sellers just by multiplying accounts. Like a quill signing a ledger, every action stays traceable to the bonded identity.
